The intended "dictionary order, case-sensitive" likely ASCII/byte order: uppercase before lowercase. That gives Apple, apple, fig, pear, plum. Let me redo with LC_ALL=C to be deterministic and check.

Actually GNU sort -u with locale may give "apple" then "Apple" (as seen). With LC_ALL=C: Apple, apple, fig, pear, plum. Which one does the task want? "字典序（区分大小写）" = lexicographic order, case-sensitive. The canonical case-sensitive lexicographic ordering is byte/codepoint order where uppercase < lowercase. I'll use LC_ALL=C for determinism and explain.

Let me verify and re-run.
